shared_elements: T-shaped/rectangular pillar head carved in low relief
animal in profile carved in low relief on the pillar shaft
band or field of repeated geometric pattern (net/mesh, hatching) on the upper block
quadruped with elongated body and tail in side view
repeated small motifs in a row across the top
justification: Both surfaces are carved T-shaped monoliths where the broad upper block carries a field of repeated geometric pattern (mesh/hatched band with rows of small repeated signs) while the narrower shaft beneath bears animals shown in strict profile in shallow, flat, outlined relief, a fairly specific combined scheme. The main difference is that A shows only a single animal beneath a large net-like field, whereas B stacks several distinct creatures (a snarling quadruped, a bird-like figure, further beasts) in multiple registers plus arched motifs, making its programme far denser and more varied.
